stubs.service: LLM provider (OpenRouter chat completions API, model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5)
stubs.how: .ui-capture/llm-stub.mjs is an OpenAI/OpenRouter-compatible HTTP server loaded into the Leon server process via `node --import` (listens on 127.0.0.1:$LLM_STUB_PORT, default 4471). The profile config sets llm.providers.openrouter.base_url to it and .env has a placeholder LEON_OPENROUTER_API_KEY. It streams SSE chat-completion chunks with topic-aware answers (weather, reminders, recipes, code, summaries, translations, otherwise a contextual generic reply), fills JSON-schema structured outputs, and reports usage/cost.

stubs.service: Process listing (/bin/ps, used for stale-process cleanup)
stubs.how: .ui-capture/bin/ps prints an empty process table; the sandbox forbids executing the setuid system ps. Put first on PATH by start.sh.

stubs.service: Online update check, telemetry, pulse, context-file refresh workers
stubs.how: Not stubbed but disabled through Leon's own settings: LEON_NODE_ENV=development (skips the updater), telemetry_enabled: false, runtime.pulse_enabled: false, context.disabled_files: ['*'] (those workers need tsx IPC unix sockets, which the sandbox blocks).

app.notes: Leon's real Fastify server (server/src/index.ts run with `node --import tsx`, as `pnpm dev:server` does) serves the production build of the 2.0 web app (apps/web/dist, built with `pnpm run build:web-app`) at /web-app/ (root / is the legacy app). Toolchain via mise.toml: node 26.13.1 (.nvmrc) and pnpm 11.28.12 (the repo's devEngines asks for pnpm 12.18.0, whose Rust store lock can't be opened in the sandbox; onFail is 'ignore'). Deps installed with `pnpm install --ignore-scripts --pnpmfile .ui-capture/pnpmfile.cjs` (skips the dev-only `json` CLI package that ships a .gitmodules file the sandbox can't write; the full Python/llama.cpp setup is not needed for the UI). No auth: local profile auth is disabled by default, so the web app opens straight in as profile 'just-me'. Data: isolated LEON_HOME at .ui-capture/leon-home. On every start, .ui-capture/seed.mjs (content in seed-data.mjs) rewrites the profile's sessions in Leon's legacy archive format (sessions/index.json + <id>/conversation_log.json), which Leon's own initializeConversationArchive imports into conversations.sqlite, and adds workspaces through Leon's own workspace schema. The owner is a Lyon-based product designer and developer: 59 sessions (128 messages) spread over about 7 months, 3 pinned. 5 workspaces (Kitchen renovation (pinned), Trailhead hiking app, Lisbon March trip, Atelier Brun website freelance, Half marathon training) with briefs, folder and link resources. Rich agent turns include plans, reasoning, tool calls (weather, web search, file read/patch, ripgrep, workspace search, shell with command output, one timed-out tool error), tables, code blocks and FR/EN text. Dates are anchored to the current day at start. Main areas: sidebar with workspaces, pinned and recent sessions plus search; session feed with expandable 'worked for'/tool-call disclosures and tool detail dialogs; the composer, whose model selector shows OpenRouter / Claude Sonnet 5.5 (sending a message runs the real agent loop against the stub); the new-session page; settings (/web-app/settings) with tool/skill catalogs and connections.

prompt:
This is a checkout of leon-ai/leon (https://github.com/leon-ai/leon) at commit 677a516850a7. 🧠 Leon is your open-source personal assistant.

I want to see its user interface in a desktop browser, in the state a real, established user would see it. Please get the app running locally with its main interface working and realistic data in it.

# Running it
- Follow the repo's own setup docs and tooling. Take the simplest route that shows the real app: a static production build if the front end works without a backend, otherwise the app's own server (production or dev mode).
- If it needs a database or other services, run them locally with an embedded or file-based option (SQLite, in-memory, JSON files, an embedded Postgres such as PGlite) or the app's demo/mock mode.
- Don't redesign or restyle anything. Change only what's needed to build and run it.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):
- Give the required variables placeholder values so the app starts.
- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). Docker isn't available. A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4412 (e.g. 5412) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4412 is stopped before I check.

# When you're done, leave this in ./.ui-capture/
- app.json: {"mode": "static" or "server", "entry": "/path where the main UI opens", "login": null or {"username": "...", "email": "...", "password": "..."}, "stubs": [{"service": "what was faked", "how": "how"}], "notes": "how you set it up, what data is loaded, and the main areas of the app"}
- static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4412/ (it gets PORT=4412). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

# Order of work
You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
1. Get the app building and running with its stubs, and write the contract above (app.json plus out/ or start.sh), even if it has only a little data so far.
2. Then build out the data, re-running your seed and checking the app still loads after each substantial step, so that a working state with the data loaded so far is always in place.
Write large data sets with a short generator script rather than as one long literal file.
